## A whole new board, and it only took four different color settings to get there

SquachWatch now runs on the AWOK 2.4" board (JustCallMeKoko's ESP32-Marauder V6.1 hardware) — full credit to **bkbroiler**, who did the original pin-mapping and touch-calibration groundwork this port is built on. It's a genuinely different chip family from the CYD boards (WROOM-32, not the usual CYD pinout), with touch sharing the display's own SPI bus instead of getting its own peripheral, so it needed its own calibration approach entirely — this board drives touch through the display driver's own built-in calibration instead of the raw-sensor math the other boards use.

The color situation deserves its own paragraph. Getting this board's colors right took cycling through RGB order, color inversion, and every combination of the two, because it turns out the firmware had a line that silently overrode the color-inversion setting no matter what any individual board's config file said — so I spent a while turning a dial that was disconnected from anything. Once that was found, the actual fix took one line. This is now fixed for good, and the lesson has been extensively commented directly in the code so nobody, including me, does that again.

The web flasher now has a board picker instead of only supporting one device, and the release pipeline builds and publishes both boards every time from here on.

### The actually-useful part
- **Added**: full support for the AWOK 2.4" board (ESP32-Marauder V6.1) — new build environment, its own display/touch config, TFT_eSPI-native touch calibration, real hardware-confirmed colors. No rotate button on this one; its case only holds the panel one way.
- **Added**: a board picker on the web flasher (skizzophrenic.github.io/SquachWatch-CYD) — pick 2.8" CYD or AWOK 2.4" before installing
- **Fixed**: found and killed a real bug where a board's own color-inversion setting was being silently overridden elsewhere in the firmware — affects future board ports more than anything you'd have noticed today
- **Fixed**: the CLEAR screen's detection counters now split across however many rows the current screen orientation actually needs (2 in landscape, up to 4 in portrait) instead of a fixed layout that clipped the first entry clean off a narrow portrait screen
- **Fixed**: long speech bubble lines now wrap onto a second line instead of running off both edges of a narrow screen
